transcript_tail.text: `jq` choked on a control char in one of the issue bodies. Trying with `gh`'s built-in `--jq`.
Now to undo the bug's side effect: the original buggy call moved `FamilyFund-archive#9` to In Progress. Reverting it.

Board state now correct:

| URL | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `dstrader-aws#9` | **In Progress** (claimed) |
| `dstrader-aws#15` | Todo (newly filed: prod-server origin swap) |
| `FamilyFund-archive#9` | Todo (reverted — was wrongly set by the bug) |

**Bug found in `~/.claude/skills/start-work/scripts/agent_claims.sh`** (lines 251-252, also affects `cmd_claim` and `cmd_release` via the same lookup):

```bash
item_id="$("$GH" project item-list "$proj" --owner "$owner" --limit 200 --format json 2>/dev/null \
    | "$JQ" -r --argjson n "$issue" '.items[] | select(.content.number==$n) | .id // empty' | head -1)"
```

It picks the project item by `.content.number` only. Two repos with the same issue # on the same board (e.g. `dstrader-aws#9` + `FamilyFund-archive#9`) → wrong item gets the status edit (and silently the "wrong" claim/release status moves). It also caps at `--limit 200` (you have more than 200 items on board #1).

Fix would be: filter by `.content.url` (encodes repo+number) and bump the limit, in both `cmd_set_status` and any other spot that resolves item-id. Want me to patch the script? It's a one-spot edit but it's tooling shared across the start/close/resume-work skills, so the change touches the helper that every claim flow goes through.

End of turn: claim now correctly anchored on `dstrader-aws#9`, prod work split out to `#15`, and the tooling bug that scrambled it is documented and ready to patch on your say-so.
